title: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset B) — Four-class ASME BCI: investigation of the feasibility and comparison of two strategies for multiclassing
description: EEG dataset from 15 healthy participants performing an auditory stream segregation multiclass ERP (ASME) brain-computer interface task. Two four-class strategies were compared: ASME-4stream (four streams, one target stimulus each) and ASME-2stream (two streams, two target stimuli each). Recordings comprise 64-channel EEG plus EOG during oddball target counting. Offline binary classification and BCI simulation with linear discriminant analysis yielded average accuracies of 0.83 and 0.86 for the two strategies.
methods_description: Participants completed 12 runs alternating between ASME-4stream (SOA 0.15 s, 600 stimuli per trial) and ASME-2stream (SOA 0.3 s, 300 stimuli per trial), with 4 trials per run of about 90 s. EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz from 64 passive Ag/AgCl electrodes (BrainAmp, right mastoid reference) with horizontal and vertical EOG. Workload was assessed with the NASA-TLX questionnaire. Analysis used shrinkage-LDA on mean amplitudes from 10 intervals with chronological cross-validation.
